summary: Learn WBGT assessment, heat controls, acclimatisation, and emergency planning. Explore this practical heat stress prevention course.
lede: Occupational heat stress management covers assessing worker exposure and planning controls as workplace weather conditions change. Designed for OHS managers, site supervisors, and occupational-health practitioners, the course covers WBGT assessment using the ISO 7243 approach, work-rest-hydration planning, acclimatisation, and worker safeguards. Participants also practise heat-illness response and keeping monitoring records to track exposure and control actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess heat exposure, set site controls, support worker health, or oversee occupational safety in outdoor and high-heat operations.
prerequisites: Prior experience in occupational health and safety, site supervision, occupational health, or workforce operations is recommended. Basic familiarity with hazard identification and workplace risk controls will help you apply the exercises. Coding is not required. Bring a laptop with Excel access if you wish to complete the digital logging exercise; no software pre-install is specified.
